paragraphs: North Wales is a region, not a single council. It takes in six council areas: the Isle of Anglesey, Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire and Wrexham. Each council runs its own fostering team under the Foster Wales name, such as Foster Wales Gwynedd or Foster Wales Flintshire, and the independent services shown above also take carers across the region. Foster Wales is the national network of the 22 council fostering services in Wales, all of them not for profit.

What councils offer varies, so compare them. Foster Wales Gwynedd describes a child's allowance of £229 to £261 a week and a carer's fee of £109 to £438 a week. Foster Wales Conwy describes an allowance of £204 to £255 a week and an enhanced fee of £250.08, with free leisure centre use and council tax relief for full-time carers. Neither page gives a year, so ask for the current figures. Across Wales as a whole, Foster Wales says the child's allowance paid by councils averages £208 to £260 a week depending on age, and that council foster carers typically receive around £400 a week in total.

The needs are local too. Gwynedd has said it wants more carers so that children can stay near their friends and school, and Flintshire has said it wants children to keep their communities and cultural backgrounds. You can enquire in Welsh or English.

For each area, see our pages for Gwynedd, Conwy, Flintshire and Wrexham, and our Wales page for the national picture. Then contact your own council's Foster Wales team and two or three of the services above, and compare training, support and pay.
